# featbit_segment (Resource)

Manages an environment-specific FeatBit Segment through the documented public API.

This resource can manage only an `environment-specific` Segment. Its `scopes`
value is exactly one fully qualified Environment RN in the form
`organization/<organization_key>:project/<project_key>:env/<environment_key>`.
Shared Segments are deliberately read-only and can be observed with
`data.featbit_segment` when their exact UUID is visible from an Environment.

Terraform owns the managed Segment's name, description, included and excluded
user keys, ordered rules and conditions, and set-valued tags. Rule and
condition order is significant; user and tag ordering is not.

Segment targeting and its Environment prerequisites are separate. This
resource writes included and excluded keys and rule payloads, but it does not
create Environment End Users or register custom End User Property metadata.
The canonical example therefore leaves direct-target lists empty and uses the
built-in `keyId` property. Configure direct targets or custom properties only
when those Environment prerequisites already exist.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "featbit_organization_key" {
  description = "FeatBit organization key used in the Environment scope RN."
  type        = string
}

locals {
  project_key     = "checkout-service"
  environment_key = "staging"
}

resource "featbit_project" "example" {
  name = "Checkout service"
  key  = local.project_key
}

resource "featbit_environment" "example" {
  project_id = featbit_project.example.id
  name       = "Staging"
  key        = local.environment_key
}

resource "featbit_segment" "example" {
  environment_id = featbit_environment.example.id
  name           = "Checkout beta users"
  key            = "checkout-beta-users"
  description    = "Users selected by a built-in key rule"
  scopes = [
    "organization/${var.featbit_organization_key}:project/${local.project_key}:env/${local.environment_key}",
  ]

  rules = [
    {
      name = "Beta user key"
      conditions = [
        {
          property = "keyId"
          operator = "IsOneOf"
          value    = jsonencode(["checkout-beta-user"])
        },
      ]
    },
  ]

  tags = ["beta", "checkout"]
}
```

The `environment_id` reference creates the dependency on the parent
Environment. Supply the organization key from your deployment without putting
an access token or runtime object UUID in configuration.

## Lifecycle

- `name`, `description`, targeting, and tags update in place through their
  specialized public endpoints.
- Removing targeting values or destroying the Segment never deletes
  Environment End Users or End User Property metadata.
- `environment_id`, `key`, or `scopes` changes require replacement.
- Create refuses active or archived exact-key collisions. A shared or
  contradictory remote definition is never adopted for mutation.
- Destroy first checks exact Feature Flag references and refuses to edit those
  flags. After references are removed, it archives, permanently deletes, and
  proves exact absence in complete active and archived views.
- Ambiguous mutations execute once; confirmed server state is preserved for
  safe recovery.

## Schema

### Required

- `environment_id` (String) Immutable parent Environment UUID.
- `key` (String) Immutable exact case-sensitive Segment key within the Environment.
- `name` (String) Segment display name, updated in place.
- `scopes` (Set of String) Exactly one immutable, fully qualified Environment resource RN.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Segment description, canonicalized to an empty string when omitted and updated in place.
- `excluded_users` (Set of String) Exact user keys explicitly excluded from the Segment. Ordering is not significant.
- `included_users` (Set of String) Exact user keys explicitly included in the Segment. Ordering is not significant.
- `rules` (Attributes List) Ordered Segment rules. Provider-created rule and condition UUIDs are deterministic. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules))
- `tags` (Set of String) Segment tags. Ordering is not significant.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Segment UUID.
- `type` (String) Fixed Segment type. Managed resources are always `environment-specific`.

<a id="nestedatt--rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules`

Required:

- `conditions` (Attributes List) Ordered conditions combined with logical AND. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules--conditions))
- `name` (String) Rule display name.

Read-Only:

- `id` (String) Stable rule UUID.

<a id="nestedatt--rules--conditions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules.conditions`

Required:

- `operator` (String) Exact documented Segment condition operator.
- `property` (String) Exact user property name.
- `value` (String) Operator value. Multi-value operators use a JSON string array; IsTrue and IsFalse require an empty string.

Read-Only:

- `id` (String) Stable condition UUID.

## Import

Import an environment-specific Segment with its Environment UUID and Segment
UUID:

```shell
terraform import featbit_segment.example '<environment_uuid>/<segment_uuid>'
```

Both components must use 8-4-4-4-12 hexadecimal UUID form. Import does not make
a shared Segment mutable; refresh rejects a shared type or incompatible scope.
